lesson.title: Fractions as Division
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 6, Session 2
lesson.footer: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 2

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 5 (VC2M5N07): division with efficient written strategies, expressing results as decimals or fractions; connecting fractions, division and decimals
plan.shape: example-first: sharing pizzas shows a fraction is a division, then the teacher models the division bracket and the reverse, decimal to fraction
plan.criticalFeature: a fraction is a division: 3/8 means 3 divided by 8
decisionPoints: the choice check: 0.25 in simplest form
plan.anchor: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Show 23 squares on a hundred grid: 23/100 = 0.23, then start at the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
Under it: a fraction is a division, 3/8 = 3 divided by 8

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Division-bracket decimals, a fraction table, decimals to simplest fractions, a mistake, and sharing problems.
resources.title: Fractions as Division
resources.subtitle: A fraction is a division. Decimals go back to fractions out of 10, 100 or 1000.

example.prompt: Write 1/4 as a decimal by dividing.

items.prompt: Write each fraction as a decimal. Divide, or make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000.

example.prompt: Write 0.45 as a fraction in simplest form.

items.prompt: Write each as a fraction in simplest form.
Ella wrote 0.6 as a fraction. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.answer: The 6 is in the tenths place: 0.6 = 6/10 = 3/5.

example.prompt: 4 friends share 3 pizzas equally. How much each?

items.prompt: 5 friends share 3 pizzas equally. How much does each get, as a fraction and a decimal?
A 7 m rope is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Decimals that repeat, mixed numbers and a sharing puzzle, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Repeating Decimals
resources.subtitle: Some divisions never stop.

steps: 3 into 10 is 3 r 1 again, and again.

items.prompt: Write 2/3 as a decimal. What do you notice?
Write 1/9, 2/9 and 4/9 as decimals. What is the pattern?
Divide to find out: does each decimal stop, or repeat forever?
Predict 7/9 as a decimal without dividing. Then check by dividing.
Write each as a mixed number and as a decimal.

example.prompt: 6 kids share 9 oranges. How many each?

items.prompt: A coach has 15 litres of sports drink to share equally among 8 players. How much does each player get? Show it as a fraction, a mixed number and a decimal.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: the bracket set up for you, tenths and hundredths, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Fractions and Division: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Top number divided by bottom number.

slides.notes: Session 2 of our fractions, decimals and percentages week: today we see that a fraction is a division.

Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and write 'a fraction is a division' under the anchor. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Expected results
prompts: P(blue) = 1/5. In 60 spins, how many blues would you expect?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with probability and area.
ASK: How many blues would you expect in 60 spins?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> one fifth of 60: share 60 into 5 groups. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One fifth of 60 is 12. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 300.
Fix: say 'one fifth of', and they divide.
notes.prep: Review of Week 4 probability (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Relative frequency
prompts: 18 heads in 40 tosses. Write it as a percentage.

beats: ASK: What is 18 heads in 40 tosses, as a percentage?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 45%
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> halve both to get 9/20, then make it out of 100. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 18 out of 40 is 45 out of 100,
so 45 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 18%.
Fix: ask what the total is, and they make it out of 100.

beats: ASK: What is the area of this rectangle?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 80 m²
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> say area covers the inside: length times width. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 16 times 5 is 80 square metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 42, the perimeter.
Fix: say area covers, and they multiply.

beats: SAY: Now for our eight times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 8 times 6?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 48
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double, double, double: 12, 24, 48. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 48. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 42 or 54.
Fix: double 6 three times: 12, 24, 48, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's a bigger one.
ASK: What is 8 times 12?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 96
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 8 tens plus 8 twos. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 96. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 86.
Fix: 8 tens is 80, 8 twos is 16, add them, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many eights make 56?
ASK: What is 56 divided by 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in eights to 56. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 7. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 6 or 8.
Fix: check: 7 eights is 56, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to use division to write fractions as decimals, and to write decimals as fractions.
successCriteria: I can say a fraction as a division: 3/8 means 3 divided by 8.
I can divide to write a fraction as a decimal.
I can write a decimal as a fraction in its simplest form.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we made fractions out of 10 or 100.
Today we find a way that works for any fraction: division.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 fraction as division is reachable for everyone; SC2 dividing to a decimal is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 decimal to simplest fraction is the stretch.

slides.title: Share the pizzas
slides.prompt: 4 friends share 3 pizzas equally. How much does each get?

beats: POINT to the pizzas.
SAY: Here are 3 pizzas, and 4 hungry friends who share them equally.
ASK: How much pizza does each friend get?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/4 of a pizza
SCAN boards for 3/4.
80%+ -> cold call one student: How did you share them?
Less -> draw each pizza cut into quarters and hand them out. Re-ask.
SAY: Each friend gets three quarters. 3 pizzas divided by 4 people is 3/4.
So a fraction is a division. That's today's big idea.
trap: writing 4/3 or 1 each.
Fix: cut each pizza into quarters and share, and they recount.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: sharing shows 3/4 = 3 divided by 4. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A fraction whose top and bottom have no common factor except 1.

beats: POINT to the words.
SAY: These words are simplest form. Say them with me: sim-plest form.
SAY: A fraction is in simplest form when
nothing divides into both the top and the bottom,
except 1. So 75/100 simplifies to 3/4.
ASK: Is 6/10 in simplest form? Thumbs up for yes, down for no.
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs down: 3/5
trap: stopping at 6/10.
Fix: ask what divides into 6 and 10, and they simplify.
notes.prep: Simplest form is the finish line for decimal-to-fraction work.

slides.title: A fraction is a division
steps: 8 into 3 does not go: write 0 and the point.
8 into 30 is 3 r 6; 60 is 7 r 4; 40 is 5.

beats: POINT to 3/8.
SAY: 3/8 means 3 divided by 8,
so I set it up with the division bracket.
I write 3 with some zeros after the point.
MODEL each step.
SAY: 8 into 3 won't go, so 0 and a point.
8 into 30 is 3, remainder 6.
8 into 60 is 7, remainder 4. 8 into 40 is 5. So 0.375.
ASK: Use the bracket. What is 1/8 as a decimal?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.125
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 1 divided by 8 is 0.125.
Eighths need three decimal places.
trap: dividing 8 by 3.
Fix: say top divided by bottom, and they set it up again.
notes.help: Write the zeros first: 1.000 under the bracket.
notes.prep: The critical feature: a fraction is a division. SC1 and SC2.

slides.title: Decimal to fraction
steps: Find a number that divides both: 5.
Nothing else divides 9 and 20: simplest form.

beats: POINT to the grid.
SAY: Now the other way. 0.45 is 45 hundredths, so I write 45 over 100.
MODEL simplifying.
SAY: 5 divides into both 45 and 100: that gives 9/20.
Nothing else divides into 9 and 20, so it's in simplest form.
ASK: How do you write 0.8 as a fraction in simplest form?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4/5
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 0.8 is 8 tenths, 8/10, which simplifies to 4/5.
trap: writing 8/100.
Fix: point to the tenths place, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Write 0.875 as a fraction in simplest form.
notes.help: Write the place value name first: 8 tenths.
notes.prep: Read the place value, then simplify. SC3.

slides.title: 0.25 in simplest form
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: uses tenths for a hundredths decimal
reads the digits 2 and 5 as the top and bottom

beats: SAY: Read the place value first, then simplify.
ASK: What is 0.25 as a fraction in simplest form?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What is 2/5 as a decimal?
Less -> shade 25 on a hundred grid and see a quarter. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A: 25/100 simplifies to 1/4.
B used tenths, and C read the digits as a fraction.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: work out 2 divided by 5, 0.4, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. B: place value; C: digits read as a fraction.

slides.title: Switch the name
slides.ask: Write it in the other form.
slides.pivot: fraction to decimal: divide; decimal to fraction: read the place
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How did you check it?

say: Let's practise switching between fractions and decimals.
Write each answer on your board.
trap: forgetting to simplify.
Fix: ask what divides into both, and they simplify.
notes.stretch: Write each one as a percentage too.
notes.help: Use the division bracket for fractions to decimals.
notes.prep: Guided practice both ways, ending with a fraction greater than 1. SC2 and SC3.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Read the place value carefully.
ASK: How do you write 0.06 as a fraction in simplest form?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/50
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> write 0.06 into the place value chart: 6 hundredths. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 6 hundredths is 6/100, which simplifies to 3/50. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 6/10.
Fix: point to the hundredths place, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone writing 6/10 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Switch between fractions and decimals on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which way are you switching, and how?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: dividing the bottom by the top.
Fix: say top divided by bottom, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: repeating decimals, mixed numbers and a sharing puzzle.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: the bracket set up for you, and tenths first.
notes.prep: Independent practice: dividing, a fraction table, decimals to fractions, a mistake and sharing. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: How do you write 7/8 as a decimal?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.875
RECORD who divides the wrong way or stops early.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing 1.142 (8 divided by 7).
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: eighths need three places.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner why a fraction is a division.

notes.answer: open - listen for 3/8 means 3 shared into 8 parts: 3 divided by 8
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can switch between fractions and decimals?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 1.142 on the board matters most.
ASK: Why is a fraction a division?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: 3/8 means 3 shared into 8 parts: 3 divided by 8
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: percentages.
